Lift shadows are pseudo-element layers whose opacity changes; the paper grain is one 128 px tile generated once with canvas2d.
Prints are inline SVG (the halftone moon is a single path) with reserved 4:5 aspect ratios, so nothing shifts while the feed renders.
All other motion is WAAPI or Motion springs on transform and opacity; every running animation is cancelled on unmount or on the next input.
The simulated server uses timers only; all of them are cleared on unmount.
demos.dataNote: Sample content: Ines Varga, Tidewater Print Club, Wrenmouth, every comment and every like/follower count are fictional. Requests go to an in-memory simulated server with ~0.7 s latency; nothing leaves the page.

demos.name: Interactive Poll
demos.summary: A community radio station’s listener polls under a tuning dial you can really turn: a single-choice poll whose rows become result bars, a multiple-choice poll with honest percentages and clearly labelled simulated live votes you can pause, a no-timer quiz with explanations, and a ranking poll whose ballot is a drag-to-reorder running order.
highlights: The FM dial is a real tuner: drag or click the band and the needle follows with a pull into each 0.2 MHz detent; throw it and a release spring carries the velocity into the nearest detent, with a magnetic catch on 98.2. A signal meter (the same lit segments as the results) and a readout answer continuously; off-station it says so and offers “Back to 98.2”. Keyboard: ←/→, Page Up/Down, Home/End.

Single choice adapts the poll-result-bars technique flat inside the station’s cue card (no card in a card): rows turn into bars in place on the heavy glide spring, staggered, with percentages counting up; largest-remainder rounding, “Your vote” in words, one polite announcement, change your vote.

Multiple choice states its promises up front (results after voting, a real closing time) and explains why “of respondents” percentages don’t add up to 100; result segments light in a sweep. Simulated live tallies are labelled as generated in your browser, finite (40 votes), pausable, and start paused under reduced motion.
Lit from one top-left light: cue cards carry a two-layer shadow; every option row and button lifts on hover, presses below rest and springs back, and a chosen option sits pressed in.

Quiz: one question at a time, no timer, the same button turns from Check answer into Next question so focus never jumps; feedback is words and a mark, not colour. Ranking composes drag-reorder-list as the ballot (pointer drag with lift and spring, or Space + arrows + Space).
accessibility: The tuning dial is a slider with value text (“98.2 megahertz, Quay FM” / “92.4 megahertz, no station”), a visible focus ring and full keyboard control; the settled position is announced politely, never every frame.
Each poll is a fieldset with its question as the legend; options are native radios or checkboxes with 48 px rows and a visible focus ring.

After voting, focus moves to “Change vote” or the results heading; changing the answer returns focus to the options. Results are announced once, politely; bars are aria-hidden and every row carries its label, percentage and tags as text.
The ranking ballot has a full keyboard path (Space to pick up, ↑/↓ to move, Space to drop, Esc to cancel) and the results are an ordered list.
demos.reducedMotion: The needle jumps to each detent (dragging still follows the pointer); result bars appear at their final width with a 160 ms fade and the numbers are shown at once; meter segments switch without a sweep; buttons and options change shadow and fill without moving; simulated live votes start paused (Resume is still available); the ranking rows swap without gliding.
performance: The dial writes the needle transform, the readout and 12 segment attributes directly while it moves; React only re-renders when the detent changes.
Result bars are transform-only WAAPI animations on full-width fills in clipped tracks; the count-up reads each bar’s progress in one rAF loop that runs only while bars move.
Meters are plain elements toggled by data attributes; the simulation updates React state once per 1.4 s and stops itself after 40 votes.
demos.dataNote: Sample content: Quay FM, The Early Edit and every count are fictional — 1,269 sample votes on the reading-spot poll, 640 sample respondents, 312 sample ballots, and live votes generated in the browser from a seeded random sequence. The dial plays nothing. Nothing is sent anywhere.

demos.name: Stories
demos.summary: Mobile-first stories for a fictional harbour town: a tray of accounts that opens into a full-screen viewer with segmented progress, tap zones, hold to pause, swipes between accounts and down to close — every one mirrored by a button and a key — on a desktop stage that takes the colour of the story, plus a story embedded in the page.
highlights: Signature: the ring you press grows into the viewer (a circular reveal from the ring’s own position) and the viewer closes back into it, faster than it opened.

A desktop stage, not just a phone in a void: a device with a lit bezel, a room that takes the colour of the card on screen (a registered colour property, so it blends between cards), the neighbouring accounts waiting on either side as dimmed peek cards you can click, and the keys set out as keycaps under the phone.

The page itself is composed for wide screens: masthead, tray and the gesture guide on the left, the embedded story on a lit stage on the right. The guide is a set of designed hints — a pictogram of each gesture with its button and keycaps — instead of a table.
The current progress segment’s animation is the clock (the story-progress-segments technique): pausing it pauses the story; it stops for the Pause button, a held press, reply focus and a hidden tab.

Gestures with twins: tap left/right ↔ Previous/Next card buttons and ←/→; swipe sideways ↔ peek cards, account buttons and Shift+←/→; hold ↔ Pause and Space; swipe down ↔ Close and Esc. Swipes follow the finger with resistance at the ends and commit past 30 % or 0.5 px/ms; short of that the card springs back. Tap zones mirror in right-to-left layouts.

Every control has depth: rings lift and press, head buttons, card arrows, Send and the account buttons lift on hover and press in on a token spring. A natural end: after the last account the viewer says “You’re all caught up” and nothing else plays.
accessibility: The viewer is a modal dialog contained in the demo: the page behind is inert and does not scroll, focus starts on Pause and returns to the ring that opened it; the dialog is described by the keyboard keys.
Each card is a labelled group (“Card 2 of 3 from Ellery Bakery, 3 h ago”) with real text; drawings have their own descriptions. Manual moves are announced politely, automatic ones are not.
Peek cards are real buttons named “Previous account: …” / “Next account: …”; the gesture guide is a list of text with decorative pictograms.
The reply field is labelled, pauses the story while focused, and states that replies are private.
All controls are 44 px or larger; focus rings turn flag-yellow on the dark viewer so they keep contrast.
demos.reducedMotion: No clock at all: cards never advance on their own (the Pause button is not needed and is removed), progress shows position statically, the viewer opens and closes with a 160 ms fade instead of the reveal, account changes cross-fade in 160 ms instead of sliding, the stage changes colour without blending, controls change fill without moving, and the embedded story waits for its step buttons.
performance: Cards are DOM and inline SVG — nothing to download or preload, so the progress never runs ahead of content.
One WAAPI animation per visible card drives the clock; the open and close reveal is one clip-path animation; transforms only for drags and transitions; everything is cancelled on close.
The stage colour is a single registered custom property transition; peek cards and controls animate transform and opacity only.
demos.dataNote: Sample content: Port Ellery, its accounts, notices, times and the “214 hours” figure are fictional. Replies are not sent anywhere.
